subproblem.title: For an integer multiplicity current on ℝ^P and closed F: spt T ⊆ F iff R.measure(Fᶜ) = 0
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) and let R be an integer multiplicity representation (IMRep univ n) with R.Represents T. Let F ⊆ ℝ^P be closed. Then spt T ⊆ F if and only if R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ F) = 0, where R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M is the weight measure (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier).withDensity R.mult.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (F : Set (Euclid P)), R.Represents T → IsClosed F → (T.support ⊆ F ↔ R.measure Fᶜ = 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 (b) of the parent proof (R_T.measure(ℝ^P ∖ spt T) = 0 via imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null) and Step 6 of the parent proof ("If x ∉ F, choose ε > 0 with ball(x, ε) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ F; then R_B.measure(ball(x, ε)) = 0, so x ∉ spt B by dimred_im_mass_measure (b)"), combined into one equivalence.
Accepted results cited by name (dependencies of ancestors of this node): imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null (∀ P n U T R, IsOpen U → R.Represents T → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ T.support) = 0) and dimred_im_mass_measure (its part (b): ∀ x ∈ U, x ∈ T.support ↔ ∀ ε > 0, R.measure (ball x ε) ≠ 0, for IsOpen U and R.Represents T).
Write σ := R.measure = (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier).withDensity (x ↦ R.mult x).

1. (spt T)ᶜ is open. Since the domain is ℝ^P, spt T = ℝ^P ∖ Z(T), where Z(T) = T.zeroRegion; hence (spt T)ᶜ = Z(T), which is open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion, a union of open sets). In particular (spt T)ᶜ is a Borel set.
2. σ((spt T)ᶜ) = 0. By imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null, applied with U = ℝ^P (open) and R representing T, μHE[n](R.carrier ∖ spt T) = 0. Because (spt T)ᶜ is measurable, (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier)((spt T)ᶜ) = μHE[n]((spt T)ᶜ ∩ R.carrier) = μHE[n](R.carrier ∖ spt T) = 0. A measure with density is absolutely continuous with respect to its base measure (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous), so σ((spt T)ᶜ) = 0.
3. (⇒) Assume spt T ⊆ F. Then Fᶜ ⊆ (spt T)ᶜ, so by monotonicity and step 2, σ(Fᶜ) ≤ σ((spt T)ᶜ) = 0, i.e. σ(Fᶜ) = 0.
4. (⇐) Assume σ(Fᶜ) = 0 and let x ∈ spt T. Suppose, for contradiction, that x ∉ F. Since F is closed, Fᶜ is open, so there is ε > 0 with ball(x, ε) ⊆ Fᶜ (Metric.isOpen_iff); hence σ(ball(x, ε)) ≤ σ(Fᶜ) = 0. On the other hand dimred_im_mass_measure, part (b), applied with U = ℝ^P (open), R representing T and x ∈ ℝ^P, states that x ∈ spt T if and only if σ(ball(x, ε')) ≠ 0 for every ε' > 0; as x ∈ spt T, σ(ball(x, ε)) ≠ 0, a contradiction. Hence x ∈ F, and spt T ⊆ F. ∎
proof_key_steps: (spt T)ᶜ = zeroRegion T is open, hence Borel.
μHE[n](carrier ∖ spt T) = 0 (imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null) gives (H^n⌞carrier)((spt T)ᶜ) = 0, so σ((spt T)ᶜ) = 0 by absolute continuity of withDensity.
(⇐) for x ∈ spt T ∖ F pick ball(x, ε) ⊆ Fᶜ; σ(ball) = 0 contradicts dimred_im_mass_measure (b).

audit.reason: Both directions are proved for the exact hypotheses. Carrier-nullity and absolute continuity give concentration on support; monotonicity proves the forward implication. Closedness of F supplies the ball needed for the reverse implication using the accepted support criterion.
